records.justification: The agent's text captures the purpose and priority theme of the funding opportunity but omits the information about the typical duration of the funding.

claims.text: The funding is for research on racial diversity within the UK.
The research should focus on barriers and pathways to a racially just and inclusive society.
The 2026 priority theme is inter-generational changes, continuities and challenges in a racially diverse UK.
Funding duration is usually between six months and three years.

records.justification: The agent's text accurately reflects the purpose, deadlines, and funding amounts mentioned in the page text. It also correctly identifies that projects must align with priority questions and aim to improve lives in the UK, and that UK-based organizations are generally required.

claims.text: Funding is available for research projects that address one or more of the Foundation's five priority questions.
The research funded aims to improve lives in the UK.
There are two application deadlines a year, in spring and autumn.
The maximum grant amount is £500,000, with exceptions up to £750,000.
Most grants awarded are below £300,000.
The outline application deadline is 5 October 2026.
Projects led by organisations or institutions not based in the UK are generally not funded.

records.justification: All claims made in the agent's text are directly supported by the provided page text.

claims.text: The funding opportunity is for research to understand the barriers and pathways to a racially just and inclusive society in the UK.
The priority theme for 2026 applications is inter-generational changes, continuities and challenges in a racially diverse UK.
Grants are available from £15,000 to £500,000.
The next deadline for applications is October 5, 2026.
The fund supports research on racial diversity within the UK.
The fund focuses on or incorporates themes of racial inequalities, discrimination, and pathways to racial justice.
The fund particularly welcomes applications that take an intersectional approach.
There is one deadline a year for this fund, in the Autumn.

records.justification: All claims made in the agent's text are directly supported by the provided page text, covering the nature of the grants, their purpose, funding amounts, eligibility criteria, and the process for checking proposal fit.

claims.text: The funding is for research grants.
The grants are for original, ambitious, and transformative projects.
The projects should confront the scale and urgency of the UK's biggest social and economic challenges.
The projects must address one or more of five priority questions.
Up to £15 million is available.
Grants are typically in the range of £1-3 million each.
Proposals should combine rigorous research with a clear focus on impact.
The fund is particularly keen to fund multidisciplinary work.
The fund is particularly keen to fund experimental and innovative approaches.
The aim of the funding is improving people's lives in the UK.
Proposals must be relevant to at least one of the priority questions.
There must be a clear path to how the research might make a difference to people's lives.
The research methodology must be appropriate and rigorous.
The research should incorporate multidisciplinary perspectives.
The team must have appropriate experience, expertise, and potential.
The team must have the capacity to manage large, complex projects.
The budget requested must be appropriate and offer good value for money.
Individuals without formal employment or other relationship with the institution hosting the grant will not be funded.
Projects led by individuals unaffiliated to any particular organisation will not be funded.
Projects led by undergraduates or master’s students will not be funded.
PhD fees or projects where the main purpose is to support a PhD will not be funded.
The establishment of academic posts will not be funded.
Ongoing costs will not be funded.
The costs of ‘rolling out’ existing work or services will not be funded.
Prospective applicants can send a one-page summary of their proposal to strategicfund@nuffieldfoundation.org to check for potential fit.
Summaries must be submitted before February 1st, 2026, to be reviewed.
